Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

Usage:
  entire session attach <session-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -a, --agent string     Agent that created the session (see 'entire agent list' for registered agents, including external) (default "claude-code")
  -f, --force            Skip confirmation and amend the last commit with the checkpoint trailer (best-effort; if the amend fails the checkpoint is still created and the trailer is printed for manual paste)
  -h, --help             help for attach
      --review           Tag the attached session as an agent review
      --skills strings   Optional: declare which review skills were run in this session. Only used with --review

content.text:
All 7 earlier sessions for this project are now linked to Entire. They sit in one checkpoint, `01M4MNZNFW7Y45HE42T5RNJW6G`. I confirmed it shows up in `entire checkpoint list`, but I haven't opened it to check the contents.

- **Why it was empty:** Entire only creates a checkpoint when a commit is made while its hooks are running. The hooks were installed after your earlier sessions, so none of them were captured. This session is tracked by the hooks and will get its own checkpoint at your next commit.
- **The commit:** the sessions attach by amending a commit with a checkpoint trailer. The last commit was already pushed, so I committed your staged `.entire/.gitignore` as a new local commit (`14a7ac8`) and attached the sessions to that. I didn't amend or force-push anything.
- **Sessions attached:** `ca16dfff`, `a90c10a4`, `3831dbbb`, `0c2230b2`, `5f614e2a`, `6a9a52ee` and `d0e5cd50`, with 1 to 20 turns each.
- **Push still needed:** `main` is one commit ahead of `origin/main`. Push when you're ready, and the checkpoint will sync to the remote then.
- **Other projects:** I only did this repo. Your other projects under `~/.claude/projects` (TechEU, cellvara, kicad and so on) need Entire enabled in their own repos. Then I can run the same `entire session attach` loop there if you want.
